lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Pluto, we can't put up with Menippus here — this dog — as our neighbour any longer. Either relocate him somewhere else, or we're moving.
lines.description: formal complaint, sincerely outraged and grandiose

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: What's so terrible? He's just as dead as you are.

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: Whenever we groan and lament — remembering what we had up there: Midas here his gold, Sardanapalus his luxuries, me, Croesus, my treasuries — he laughs at us. He calls us names. Slaves. Garbage. And sometimes he actually sings, [pause] right over our weeping, just to spoil it. The man is unbearable.
lines.description: building indignation; wounded dignity, escalating list

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Entirely true, Pluto. I despise them. They're contemptible little wretches. It wasn't enough to have lived badly — now they're dead and they're still clinging to it, still pining for the world upstairs. So yes, I enjoy needling them.
lines.description: cheerfully candid, amused rather than defensive

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Well, you shouldn't. They're grieving real losses.
lines.description: mild reprimand, procedural fairness with a sigh

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Pluto. Don't tell me you're siding with their snivelling.

lines.speaker: Pluto
lines.text: Not at all. I just don't want a feud in the building.

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Well then. You — worst of the Lydians, Phrygians, and Assyrians — get this through your skulls: I am not stopping. Wherever you go, I'll follow. Needling. Singing. Laughing.
lines.description: delighted threat, crisp and implacably cheerful

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.description: scandalized appeal, expecting the room to agree

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: No. The outrage was what you did — expecting people to bow to you, swaggering over free men, never sparing a thought for death. Well. Now you'll do your wailing, with all of it stripped away.
lines.description: dry verdict, firm but not moralizing

lines.speaker: Croesus
lines.text: [crying] Oh gods — so much, so many great possessions —
lines.description: genuine sobbing, rich man's grief laid bare

lines.speaker: Menippus
lines.text: Excellent. Keep it up. You wail; I'll accompany you. [pause] 'Know thyself' — over and over. Makes a nice refrain. Goes beautifully with that sort of lamentation.
